children.text: Serena Neel starts off her video directly stating that she “bought 50,000 damaged pickles and [she] is going to put them all in a pool and go swimming” with a tone that is enthusiastic and determined. With this type of communication, she aims to keep her viewers fixated on the how and why of her bizarre idea of content. In the background of this time frame, she pans to the boxes of the 50,000 pickles behind her to visually show the extent of the task at hand, therefore, also contributing to the hook of the video. She then explains the exact process of how they are cleaning and putting the pickles inside the pool by maintaining the same enthusiastic tone to communicate to the audience.

She explicitly explains why she bought all these pickles and the context behind it. She states that the pickles were “damaged” and that they “couldn’t be eaten” so there was “nothing you could do with them.” She then physically shows that the pickles are inedible by folding one in half causing it to explode showing the unusual softness of the pickles. This can also be an implicitly interpreted implication that her perceived purpose behind the project is to significantly help out a small business not lose out on a lot of money and also making a fun event for her surrounding community all while staying true to the normal absurdity of her content. She also most likely said this at this time to avoid any controversies over accusations of wasting pickles.

Neel records community volunteers helping out with unjarring the pickles and also shows that these damaged pickles are also being used effectively making compost. Without explicitly stating this, the true purpose of this project is to not trash these pickles and instead, positively contribute to the environment and this small business that could have lost out of a lot of money. She has clear intent of her contributions that would eventually happen behind the scenes, but she chooses to base her content on something that will grab the audience’s attention as she does in all of her content on her page.

Serena Neel is seen jumping in the now filled pickle pool, and here she is displaying her regular, true personality having a joyful time breaking an interesting, weird world record but also helping out a business and the environment. Neel is visibly showing her humor and her authentic self after finishing such a silly, bizarre task with nothing but goodwilled intent behind it thus posing her as a relatable and reliable influencer and someone to look up to. Joe, the man that owns the pickle company, also jumps in which can correlate to the importance and dedication of the actual purpose of this project if the owner is also quite entertained and determined by the results.

A drone shot records a bunch of little kids and families having fun in the pickle pool from around Neel’s neighborhood. Bringing together her community to join her in her achievement simply boosts her authenticity and credibility even more because she is providing these kids and families with a unique, lifelong memory and experience that they will likely never forget. The fact that this time frame is particularly a drone shot can also show that it is most likely not performative or staged and that these kids were simply invited to share an original experience with Serena Neel.

She is starting to put the pickles in the pool at this point and she edits this segment in a way where only the visuals of her pouring them in and the sound of them splashing into the pool are included. This use of audio and visual cues can attract the viewer and keep them more engaged. ASMR in social media has become quite an influential genre of content for influencers to utilize. By editing out the fluff that would have come between pouring each of the wheelbarrows of pickles into the pool, it filters out any potential distractions or tendencies for viewers to scroll by also providing satisfying audial and visual signals to keep the engagement.
